f.title: Plan early in the life cycle how risks will be characterised and minimised post-authorisation
f.statement: Marketing authorisation applicants are encouraged to plan from very early in a product's life cycle how they will further characterise and minimise the risks associated with the product in the post-authorisation phase.
f.clause: V.A. Introduction
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Focus the RMP on risks relevant for risk management activities
f.statement: GVP Annex I definitions apply for this Module, but the RMP should focus on those risks that are relevant for the risk management activities for the authorised medicinal product.
f.clause: V.A.1. Terminology

rows.quote: The definitions from GVP Annex I apply also for the purpose of this GVP Module. However, the RMP should focus on those risks that are relevant for the risk management activities for the authorised medicinal product.

f.title: Address in the RMP only identified risks that are undesirable clinical outcomes with sufficient evidence of causation
f.statement: From the identified risks of the medicinal product, the RMP should address only risks that are undesirable clinical outcomes and for which there is sufficient scientific evidence that they are caused by the medicinal product. Not all reported adverse reactions are necessarily a relevant risk of the product in a given therapeutic context.
f.clause: V.A.1. Terminology

rows.quote: From the identified risks of the medicinal product, the RMP should address only the risks that are undesirable clinical outcomes and for which there is sufficient scientific evidence that they are caused by the medicinal product. Reports of adverse reactions may be derived from multiple sources such as non-clinical findings confirmed by clinical data, clinical trials, epidemiological studies, and spontaneous data sources, including published literature. They may be linked to situations such as off label use, medication errors or drug interactions. Not all reported adverse reactions are necessarily considered a relevant risk of the product in a given therapeutic context.
rows.location: V.A.1. Terminology
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to cover the sentence that not all reported adverse reactions are a relevant risk.

f.title: Address in the RMP only potential risks with scientific evidence suggesting a possible causal relationship
f.statement: From the potential risks of the medicinal product, the RMP should address only risks that are undesirable clinical outcomes for which there is scientific evidence to suspect a possible causal relationship with the medicinal product, but where there is currently insufficient evidence to conclude that the association is causal.
f.clause: V.A.1. Terminology

rows.quote: From the potential risks of the medicinal product, the RMP should address only the risks that are undesirable clinical outcomes and for which there is scientific evidence to suspect the possibility of a causal relationship with the medicinal product, but where there is currently insufficient evidence to conclude that this association is causal.
rows.location: V.A.1. Terminology
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Focus the RMP on important identified risks likely to impact the risk-benefit balance
f.statement: The RMP should focus on the important identified risks that are likely to have an impact on the risk-benefit balance of the product. An important identified risk included in the RMP would usually warrant further evaluation in the pharmacovigilance plan and/or risk minimisation activities (product information advising specific clinical actions, or additional risk minimisation activities).
f.clause: V.A.1. Terminology

rows.quote: An important identified risk to be included in the RMP would usually warrant:  Further evaluation as part of the pharmacovigilance plan (e.g. to investigate frequency, severity, seriousness and outcome of this risk under normal conditions of use, which populations are particularly at risk);  Risk minimisation activities: product information advising on specific clinical actions to be taken to minimise the risk (see V.B.8.), or additional risk minimisation activities.
rows.location: V.A.1. Terminology
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: previous quote was truncated mid-sentence; the first sentence ends in a line-end hyphenated word (risk-benefit), so the quote now covers the "would usually warrant" part only and the first sentence (focus on important identified risks likely to impact the risk-benefit balance) is outside the quote although verbatim in V.A.1.

f.title: Consider adverse outcomes linked to off-label use, unstudied populations or long-term use as potential risks and include important ones
f.statement: Important potential risks to be included in the RMP are those that, when further characterised and if confirmed, would have an impact on the risk-benefit balance. Where there is a scientific rationale that an adverse clinical outcome might be associated with off-label use, use in populations not studied, or long-term use, the adverse reaction should be considered a potential risk and, if deemed important, included in the list of safety concerns as an important potential risk. Important potential risks would usually require further evaluation in the pharmacovigilance plan.
f.clause: V.A.1. Terminology

rows.quote: The important potential risks to be included in the RMP are those important potential risks that, when further characterised and if confirmed, would have an impact on the risk-benefit balance of the medicinal product. Where there is a scientific rationale that an adverse clinical outcome might be associated with off-label use, use in populations not studied, or resulting from the long-term use of the product, the adverse reaction should be considered a potential risk, and if deemed important, should be included in the list of safety concerns as an important potential risk. Important potential risks included in the RMP would usually require further evaluation as part of the pharmacovigilance plan.
rows.location: V.A.1. Terminology
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the whole paragraph so it proves the first and last sentences of the statement.

f.title: Include missing information only with a scientific rationale that the safety profile may differ
f.statement: Missing information refers to gaps in knowledge about safety for certain anticipated utilisation or particular patient populations where it is unknown whether the safety profile differs. The absence of data (e.g. exclusion of a population from clinical studies) does not automatically constitute a safety concern; risk management planning should focus on situations that might differ from the known safety profile, and a scientific rationale is needed to include a population as missing information in the RMP.
f.clause: V.A.1. Terminology

rows.quote: Missing information relevant to the risk management planning refers to gaps in knowledge about the safety of a medicinal product for certain anticipated utilisation (e.g. long-term use) or for use in particular patient populations, for which there is insufficient knowledge to determine whether the safety profile differs from that characterised so far. The absence of data itself (e.g. exclusion of a population from clinical studies) does not automatically constitute a safety concern. Instead, the risk management planning should focus on situations that might differ from the known safety profile. A scientific rationale is needed for the inclusion of that population as missing information in the RMP.
rows.location: V.A.1. Terminology
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to include the definition sentence used in the statement.

f.title: Keep the risk management system proportionate to the risks and need for post-authorisation safety data

f.title: Update the RMP throughout the product life cycle, adding, removing or reclassifying safety concerns
f.statement: The RMP is a dynamic document that should be updated throughout the life cycle of the product(s). This includes adding safety concerns where required and, as the safety profile is further characterised, removing or reclassifying safety concerns.
f.clause: V.B.1. Principles of risk management

rows.quote: The RMP is a dynamic document that should be updated throughout the life cycle of the product(s). This includes the addition of safety concerns where required, but also, as the safety profile is further characterised, the removal or reclassification of safety concerns.

rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: lifecycle Marketed -> Both (updates "throughout the life cycle", including pre-authorisation).

f.title: Remove or reclassify important potential risks when data no longer support them or strengthen the association
f.statement: Important potential risks may be removed from the safety specification (e.g. when accumulating data do not support the initial supposition, the impact is less than anticipated, or no pharmacovigilance activity can further characterise the risk), or need to be reclassified to important identified risks (e.g. when data strengthen the association with the product).
f.clause: V.B.1. Principles of risk management

rows.quote: It may be that important potential risks can be removed from the safety specification in the RMP (e.g. when accumulating scientific and clinical data do not support the initial supposition, the impact to the individual has been shown to be less than anticipated resulting in the potential risk not being considered important, or when there is no reasonable expectation that any pharmacovigilance activity can further characterise the risk), or they need to be reclassified to ‘important identified risks’ (e.g. if scientific and clinical data strengthen the association between the risk and the product).
rows.location: V.B.1. Principles of risk management
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the whole bullet. The passage is descriptive guidance ("may facilitate", "it may be that"); Permitted level and its reading as a requirement are interpretive.

f.title: Remove important identified risks that are fully characterised and appropriately managed
f.statement: In certain circumstances, where the risk is fully characterised and appropriately managed, important identified risks may be removed from the safety specification (e.g. for long-marketed products with no outstanding additional pharmacovigilance activities and/or where risk minimisation recommendations have become integrated into standard clinical practice such as treatment protocols or clinical guidelines).
f.clause: V.B.1. Principles of risk management

rows.quote: In certain circumstances, where the risk is fully characterised and appropriately managed, important identified risks may be removed from the safety specification (e.g. for products marketed for a long time for which there are no outstanding additional pharmacovigilance activities and/or the risk minimisation activities recommending specific clinical measures to address the risk have become fully integrated into standard clinical practice, such as inclusion into treatment protocols or clinical guidelines).
rows.location: V.B.1. Principles of risk management

f.title: Monitor pharmacovigilance data for new or changed risks and update the risk management system and RMP
f.statement: The applicant/marketing authorisation holder is responsible for ensuring that knowledge and understanding of the product's safety profile in clinical practice are critically reviewed. The MAH should monitor pharmacovigilance data to determine whether there are new risks, whether risks have changed or whether the risk-benefit balance has changed, and update the risk management system and the RMP accordingly. The critical review is a continuous activity reflected in PSUR data, where an RMP submission may or may not be warranted.
f.clause: V.B.2. Responsibilities for risk management
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Signal management; Benefit–risk review

rows.quote: ensuring that the knowledge and understanding on the product’s safety profile, following its use in clinical practice, are critically reviewed. The marketing authorisation holder should monitor pharmacovigilance data to determine whether there are new risks or whether risks have changed or whether there are changes to the risk-benefit balance of medicinal products [Dir Art 104(3)(e)], and update the risk management system and the RMP accordingly, as described below. The critical review of the safety profile of the product is a continuous activity and is reflected in data submitted with periodic safety update reports (PSUR) (see GVP Module VII), where an RMP submission may or may not be warranted.

f.title: Summarise significant non-clinical safety findings and their relevance to humans in module SII
f.statement: Module SII should present a high-level summary of significant non-clinical safety findings (e.g. toxicity, safety pharmacology, other toxicity-related data). Significant areas of toxicity by target organ system and their relevance to human use should normally be discussed, as should quality aspects relevant to safety (e.g. genotoxic impurities).
f.clause: V.B.5.3. RMP part II, module SII "Non-clinical part of the safety specification"

rows.quote: This RMP module should present a high-level summary of the significant non-clinical safety findings, for example:  toxicity (key issues identified from acute or repeat-dose toxicity, reproductive/developmental toxicity, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity);  safety pharmacology (e.g. cardiovascular system, including QT interval prolongation, nervous system);  other toxicity-related information or data. What constitutes an important non-clinical safety finding will depend upon the medicinal product, the target population and experience with other similar compounds or therapies in the same class. Normally, significant areas of toxicity (by target organ system) and the relevance of the findings to the use in humans should be discussed. Also, quality aspects if relevant to safety (e.g. genotoxic impurities) should be discussed.

rows.quote: Since every pack size is specifically authorised for a medicinal product, planning the number of “dosage units” within each pack and the range of pack sizes available can be considered a form of routine risk management activity. MAHs may be requested to submit an RMP with module SVII focused on the safety concern(s) evaluated in the procedure (other safety concerns included as needed), or an RMP based on a comprehensive identification of safety concerns; the competent authority decides which is most appropriate.
f.clause: V.C.1.2.1. New risk management plans at the request of a competent authority to address one or more safety concerns
f.applicability: New RMPs requested by a competent authority post-authorisation

rows.quote: The elements are the same as those applicable to a generic product where the originator product does not have an RMP (see V.C.1.1.1.). Two possible scenarios are envisaged: 1. Marketing authorisation holders may be requested to submit an RMP with a RMP module SVII focused on the safety concern(s) evaluated in the procedure. Other safety concerns should be included as needed. 2. Marketing authorisation holders may be requested to submit an RMP based on a comprehensive identification of safety concerns. It is left to the discretion of the competent authority, which is the most appropriate in given circumstances.
rows.location: V.C.1.2.1. New risk management plans at the request of a competent authority to address one or more safety concerns
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the two scenarios and the authority discretion; MAH "may be requested" (scenario choice is the authority's).

f.title: Follow the RMP elements of the original authorisation type for unsolicited post-authorisation RMPs
f.statement: An unsolicited RMP submitted in the post-authorisation phase follows the elements of the type of marketing authorisation under which the product was initially submitted (full, generic, informed consent, etc.).
f.clause: V.C.1.2.2. Unsolicited risk management plan submission in post-authorisation phase
f.applicability: Unsolicited RMP submissions post-authorisation

rows.quote: This RMP follows the elements of the type of marketing authorisation under which this medicinal product was initially submitted
rows.location: V.C.1.2.2. Unsolicited risk management plan submission in post-authorisation phase
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Submit the RMP as PDF files within the eCTD for centrally authorised products
f.statement: For centrally authorised medicinal products, the RMP should be submitted as PDF files within the eCTD submission.
f.clause: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU
f.applicability: Centrally authorised medicinal products

rows.quote: For centrally authorised medicinal products, the RMP should be submitted as PDF files within the eCTD submission.
rows.location: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Submit RMP annex 1 in XML format after the Commission decision within the specified timescale
f.statement: Following a Commission decision where the procedure involved submission of an RMP, marketing authorisation holders should submit RMP annex 1 in XML format within a specified timescale; after validation it is uploaded to an Agency database accessible to the Agency and Member State competent authorities.
f.clause: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU
f.applicability: Centrally authorised medicinal products

rows.deadline: Within the specified timescale following the Commission decision
rows.quote: Following a Commission decision where the procedure has involved the submission of an RMP, marketing authorisation holders should submit the RMP annex 1 in XML format within a specified timescale. RMP annex 1 provides the key information regarding the RMP in a structured electronic format which, following validation at the Agency, is uploaded into an Agency database that is accessible and searchable by the Agency and the competent authorities in the Member States.
rows.location: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the database upload sentence; the timescale is not specified in the source.

f.title: Follow national requirements for RMP submission of nationally authorised products
f.statement: The RMP submission system for nationally authorised medicinal products varies across Member States, and the national requirements should be followed.
f.clause: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU
f.applicability: Nationally authorised medicinal products

rows.quote: The system for nationally authorised medicinal products varies across Member States and the national requirements should be followed.
rows.location: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Submit the initial RMP with the initial marketing authorisation or via the appropriate post-authorisation procedure
f.statement: The initial RMP should be submitted as part of the initial marketing authorisation application or, if required, for products without an RMP, through the appropriate post-authorisation procedure.
f.clause: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU (page 33)

rows.quote: The initial RMP should be submitted as part of the initial marketing authorisation, or if required, for those products that do not have an RMP, through the appropriate post-authorisation procedure.
rows.location: V.C.2. Submission of a risk management plan to competent authorities in the EU (page 33)
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Submit an RMP update when safety concerns or additional PV or risk minimisation activities change
f.statement: An RMP update is expected to be submitted at any time when there is a change in the list of safety concerns, or a new or significant change in existing additional pharmacovigilance or additional risk minimisation activities (including their removal). For example, a change in study objectives, population or due date of final results, or addition of a new safety concern to educational material key messages, is expected to be reflected in an updated RMP with the procedure triggering those changes.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates

rows.deadline: At any time the change occurs; with the procedure triggering the change
rows.quote: An RMP update is expected to be submitted at any time when there is a change in the list of the safety concerns, or when there is a new or a significant change in the existing additional pharmacovigilance or additional risk minimisation activities. The significant changes of the existing additional pharmacovigilance and risk minimisation activities may include removing such activities from the RMP. For example, a change in study objectives, population or due date of final results, or addition of a new safety concern in the key messages of the educational materials would be expected to be reflected in an updated RMP with the procedure triggering those changes.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the removal clause and examples.

f.title: Consider an RMP update when routine PV beyond ADR reporting or routine risk minimisation with clinical measures changes
f.statement: An RMP update might be considered when data submitted in a procedure result, or are expected to result, in changes to routine pharmacovigilance activities beyond adverse reaction reporting and signal detection (e.g. significant change to annual enhanced safety surveillance plans), or to routine risk minimisation activities recommending specific clinical measures (e.g. adding renal function monitoring to SmPC section 4.4).
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates

rows.quote: An update of the RMP might be considered when data submitted in the procedure results or is expected to result in changes of routine pharmacovigilance activities beyond adverse reaction reporting and signal detection activities, or of routine risk minimisation activities recommending specific clinical measures to address the risk. For example, an RMP update might also be warranted with a significant change of the plans for annual enhanced safety surveillance (routine pharmacovigilance activity), or when monitoring of renal function is added as a recommendation in the Special warnings and precautions for use section 4.4 of the SmPC (routine risk minimisation activity).
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the examples; "might be considered" = Permitted.

f.title: Consider updating plans to evaluate risk minimisation effectiveness with such RMP updates
f.statement: The need to update the plans to evaluate the effectiveness of risk minimisation activities should also be considered with RMP updates triggered by changes to routine pharmacovigilance or routine risk minimisation.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates

rows.quote: The need to update the plans to evaluate the effectiveness of risk minimisation activities should also be considered with such updates.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Update the RMP if an emerging safety issue under assessment is confirmed as a risk to add to safety concerns
f.statement: When an emerging safety issue (as defined in GVP Module VI) is still under assessment, in particular a signal or potential risk that could be an important identified risk, an RMP update may be required if the issue is confirmed and the important identified or potential risk needs to be added to the list of safety concerns.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates

rows.quote: When an emerging safety issue is still under assessment (as defined in GVP Module VI), in particular in the context of a signal or potential risk that could be an important identified risk, an RMP update may be required if the emerging safety issue is confirmed and the important identified or potential risk requires to be added to the list of safety concerns in the RMP.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the whole sentence. "May be required" is conditional; Recommended level is a judgement.

f.title: Include a track-changes RMP with every update, against the latest and the current approved version
f.statement: Unless requested otherwise, a track-changes RMP document should be included with every RMP update, showing the changes introduced in the latest update (as applicable) as well as compared with the current approved version of the RMP.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates

rows.quote: Unless requested otherwise, a track-changes RMP document should be included with every RMP update, showing changes introduced in the latest update (as applicable), as well as compared with the “current” approved version of the RMP.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Treat the RMP submitted with the closing sequence as the single current approved version
f.statement: A medicinal product can only have one current approved version of an RMP. If several RMP updates are submitted during a procedure, the version considered the current approved RMP for future updates and track-changes purposes shall be the one submitted with the closing sequence of the procedure; the RMP is considered approved at the end of the procedure when all changes are acceptable.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Data integrity & records

rows.quote: A medicinal product can only have one “current” approved version of an RMP. If several updates to the RMP are submitted during the course of a procedure, the version considered as the “current” approved RMP for future updates and track-changes purposes shall be the one submitted with the closing sequence of the procedure. When an RMP update is submitted with a procedure, the RMP is considered approved at the end of the procedure, when all changes are considered acceptable.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the one-current-version and approval-at-end clauses.

f.title: Submit a new or updated RMP outside another procedure as a variation
f.statement: In the post-authorisation phase, submission of a new or updated RMP outside another regulatory procedure constitutes a variation in accordance with the Guidelines on Variations (see also the EMA Q&A on the Variations Guidelines for the centralised procedure).
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates

rows.quote: In the post-authorisation phase, submission of a new or updated RMP outside of another regulatory procedure constitutes a variation in accordance with the Guidelines on Variations10. For detailed guidance on relevant variation categories and their classification, please also refer to the EMA Practical
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended towards the Q&A reference (its title continues after the page break); "constitutes a variation" read as Mandatory.

f.title: Submit a combined RMP with separated SIII data for concurrent procedures requiring an RMP
f.statement: If a medicinal product has more than one concurrently ongoing procedure requiring an RMP, ideally a combined RMP should be submitted with appropriate separation of data in module SIII.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP management with parallel procedures
f.applicability: Products with concurrent procedures requiring RMP submission

rows.quote: If a medicinal product has more than one concurrently on-going procedure which requires submission of an RMP, ideally a combined RMP should be submitted with appropriate separation of data in RMP module SIII.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP management with parallel procedures
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed; "ideally" = Recommended.

f.title: Discuss the regulatory path for RMP updates affected by multiple procedures with the authority before submission
f.statement: The best regulatory path for an RMP update where multiple procedures may impact RMP content should be discussed with the competent authority before submission.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP management with parallel procedures
f.applicability: Products with multiple procedures potentially impacting the RMP

rows.quote: The best regulatory path for the RMP update in case of multiple procedures potentially impacting on the RMP content should be discussed with the competent authority before submission.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP management with parallel procedures
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Submit an updated RMP together with the PSUR when PSUR data require RMP changes
f.statement: If, when preparing a PSUR, changes to the RMP are needed as a result of new safety concerns or other PSUR data, an updated RMP should be submitted at the same time, and no stand-alone RMP variation is necessary.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR
f.exceptions: Does not apply to PSURs in a PSUR single assessment (PSUSA).
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Aggregate reporting; Submission operations

rows.deadline: At the same time as the PSUR
rows.quote: If, when preparing a PSUR, there is a need for changes to the RMP as a result of new safety concerns, or other data presented in the PSUR, then an updated RMP should be submitted at the same time. In this case no stand-alone RMP variation is necessary.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed; the PSUSA exception is from the next paragraph (row 0198).

f.title: Handle an RMP update unrelated to a coinciding PSUR as a stand-alone variation
f.statement: If only the timing of PSUR and RMP submissions coincides but the changes are not related, the RMP submission should be handled as a stand-alone variation.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR

rows.quote: Should only the timing for submission of both documents coincide, but the changes are not related to each other, then the RMP submission should be handled as a stand-alone variation.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Do not submit RMP updates with PSURs in a PSUSA; use another procedure or a separate variation
f.statement: In the context of a PSUR EU single assessment (PSUSA), RMP updates cannot be accepted together with the PSURs of centrally and/or nationally authorised products. MAHs should take the opportunity of another upcoming procedure to update their RMP, or alternatively submit a separate variation.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR
f.applicability: PSUR EU single assessment (PSUSA) procedures
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Aggregate reporting; Submission operations

rows.quote: However, in the context of a PSUR EU single assessment (PSUSA), submission of RMP updates cannot be accepted together with the PSURs of medicinal products (centrally and/or nationally authorised). Marketing authorisation holders should take the opportunity of another upcoming procedure to update their RMP. Alternatively, marketing authorisation holders should submit a separate variation to update their RMP.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the alternatives.

f.title: Submit RMP updates for nationally authorised products to the Member State competent authorities
f.statement: For nationally authorised medicinal products, RMP updates should be submitted to the competent authorities in the Member States for assessment.
f.clause: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR
f.applicability: Nationally authorised medicinal products

rows.quote: For nationally authorised medicinal products, RMP updates should be submitted to the competent authorities in the Member States for assessment.
rows.location: V.C.2.1. Risk management plans updates - RMP updates with the PSUR
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Submit a detailed description of the risk management system when a national competent authority imposes one
f.statement: For nationally authorised products, the national competent authority may impose on an MAH an obligation to operate a risk management system for each product (DIR Art 104(3)(c)) if there are concerns about risks affecting the risk-benefit balance; in that case it shall also oblige the MAH to submit a detailed description of the risk management system it intends to introduce.
f.clause: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network
f.applicability: Nationally authorised medicinal products with concerns affecting the risk-benefit balance

rows.actor: National competent authority; marketing authorisation holder
rows.quote: The national competent authority may impose an obligation on a marketing authorisation holder to operate a risk management system for each medicinal product, as referred to in DIR Art 104(3)(c), if there are concerns about the risks affecting the risk-benefit balance of an authorised medicinal product. In that context, the national competent authority shall also oblige the marketing authorisation holder to submit a detailed description of the risk-management system which he intends to introduce for the medicinal product concerned [DIR Art 104a(2)].
rows.location: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the may-impose sentence. The shall binds the national competent authority; the MAH submission duty follows from it.

f.title: Include only PRAC-recommended, CHMP-agreed measures as additional risk minimisation for centrally authorised products
f.statement: For centrally authorised products, only risk minimisation measures recommended by PRAC and subsequently agreed by CHMP should be included in the risk minimisation plan as additional risk minimisation activities. Additional risk minimisation measures are conditions to the marketing authorisation, with key elements detailed in annex II to the Commission decision.
f.clause: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network
f.applicability: Centrally authorised medicinal products

rows.quote: For centrally authorised medicinal products, only risk minimisation measures recommended by the PRAC and subsequently agreed by the CHMP should be included in the risk minimisation plan as additional risk minimisation activities. Additional risk minimisation measures are conditions to the marketing authorisation; key elements are detailed in annex II to the Commission decision.
rows.location: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: quote extended to the conditions-to-MA sentence.

f.title: Conditions on safe and effective use of centrally authorised products may be imposed on Member States under DIR Art 127a
f.statement: Exceptionally, certain conditions or restrictions with regard to the safe and effective use of a centrally authorised medicinal product may be imposed on the Member States through a Commission decision in accordance with DIR Art 127a, for implementation at national level.
f.clause: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network
f.applicability: Centrally authorised medicinal products
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Local PV interfaces

rows.quote: exceptionally, certain conditions or restrictions with regard to the safe and effective use of the medicinal product may be imposed to the Member States through a Commission decision in accordance with DIR Art 127a for their implementation at national level.
rows.location: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network

f.title: Competent authorities ensure same-substance holders align risk minimisation with reference product changes
f.statement: When necessary, competent authorities should ensure that all MAHs of medicinal products containing the same active substance make similar changes to their risk minimisation measures when changes are made to those of the reference medicinal product.
f.clause: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network

rows.actor: Competent authorities (with marketing authorisation holders of same-substance products)
rows.quote: When necessary, the competent authorities should ensure that all marketing authorisation holders of medicinal products containing the same active substance make similar changes to their risk minimisation measures when changes are made to those of the reference medicinal product.
rows.location: V.C.3. Assessment of the risk management plan within the EU regulatory network
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: confirmed; authority duty ("should ensure"); MAH roles inferred.

f.title: Publish public assessment reports and RMP summaries on the European and national medicines web-portals
f.statement: The Agency and Member States shall make publicly available, by means of the European medicines web-portal and the national medicines web-portals, public assessment reports and summaries of risk management plans. For centrally authorised products the Agency makes public a summary of the RMP and includes tables relating to the RMP in the EPAR, including the product information and any conditions to the marketing authorisation; national competent authorities will provide details of how they implement the transparency measures nationally.
f.clause: V.C.4. Transparency
f.systems: European medicines web-portal; national medicines web-portals

rows.actor: Agency and Member States (national competent authorities)
rows.quote: The Agency and Member States shall make publically available, by means of the European medicines web-portal and the national medicines web-portals, public assessment reports and summaries of risk management plans [REG Art 26(1)(c), DIR Art 106(c)]. For centrally authorised medicinal products the Agency:  makes public a summary of the RMP;  includes tables relating to the RMP in the EPAR including the product information and any conditions to the marketing authorisation. The national competent authorities will provide details of how they intend to implement the transparency measures at national level [by reference to DIR Art 106].
rows.location: V.C.4. Transparency
